answer: The sonnet multiplier is published, charged in oasis, and jetty lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 2377 identities would post 2231 proofs and burn roughly 87 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
